content: 1. The study by ert JD in JAMA Cardiology (2016) evaluates the cost-effectiveness of intensive blood pressure management, providing insights into its economic and clinical implications. 2. Howard K and colleagues (2010) conducted a modeled analysis in Value Health to assess the cost-effectiveness of screening and optimal management strategies for diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease. 3. Meiqari L et al. (2019) performed a systematic narrative review in Global Health Action, examining access to hypertension care and services in primary healthcare settings in Vietnam. 4. Shahaj O and colleagues (2019) conducted a meta-review in the Journal of Hypertension, focusing on supporting self-management for individuals with hypertension through quantitative and qualitative systematic reviews. 5. Kuate Defo B et al. (2019) published a systematic review and meta-analysis in the Journal of Hypertension, analyzing the burden of hypertension in Cameroon as a representation of the African context. 6. Ren M and colleagues (2020) evaluated the economic impact of using a fixed-dose combination of olmesartan and amlodipine for hypertension treatment in China, as reported in the Journal of Medical Economics. 7. Li T et al. (2015) conducted an economic evaluation in Clinical Drug Investigation, comparing clopidogrel and aspirin in patients with recent ischemic stroke and established peripheral artery disease in a Chinese setting. 8. Kawalec P et al. (2015) assessed the economic value of a single-pill combination of indapamide and amlodipine for arterial hypertension treatment in Poland, as published in Kardiologia Polska. 9. Burstrom K and colleagues (2001) analyzed health-related quality of life by disease and socioeconomic group in Sweden, as detailed in Health Policy. 10. Sullivan PW et al. (2008) explored the impact of obesity on diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and hypertension in the United States, as reported in Quality of Life Research. 11. Wang HM et al. (2008) conducted a cross-sectional survey in BMC Public Health, examining health-related quality of life among general practice patients with various chronic diseases in Germany. 12. Gad M et al. (2020) performed an economic evaluation in Value Health, supporting evidence-informed policy options for hypertension management in Ghana. 13. Salomon JA et al. (2012) measured disability weights for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2010, as published in The Lancet, to assess health outcomes from disease and injury. 14. Lunde L (2013) investigated the interchangeability of EQ-5D and 15D in economic evaluations of post-stroke patients' quality of life, as reported in the European Journal of Health Economics. 15. Huang J et al. (2017) analyzed the economic burden of heart failure in China, focusing on disease management and resource utilization, as detailed in the Journal of Medical Economics. 16. Golicki D et al. (2010) presented findings from the Polish valuation study on self-assessed health status using EQ-5D, as published in Polskie Archiwum Medycyny Wewnętrznej. 17. Cooper JT et al. He T et al.
